producing_agent.identity: Claude Fable 5 (Cursor agent, under J. Brown direction)

hypothesis: Gold is menu-relative. On a fixed (task, screen) case, enlarging the menu flips gold from noop to quotient. Any menu-blind κ is a function of (Y, q) alone and is therefore constant across menus, so it cannot match gold on both. This closes the close-out's door 1 categorically rather than at five fields, without refitting the cheap rule.
decision: Accept menu_blind_dead if at least one gold flip exists between MENU_BASE and MENU_EXT and κ_screen (menu-relative) is exact on all 34 rows. Accept menu_blind_lives if no flip exists and the frozen five-field rule is exact and collision-free under both menus. Accept no_function if κ_screen misses a row. Otherwise inconclusive. Any recorded verdict passes CI.

audit_card.target_object: The door-1 question from the close-out: can a specified κ that does not look at the menu hit a larger held-out family?
audit_card.decision: menu_blind_dead / menu_blind_lives / no_function / inconclusive, decided by the registered rule before interpretation.
audit_card.representation: Paper E suite plus 6 new cases on {0,1}^4, two menus (5 and 7 screens), five-field signatures, menu-relative gold.
audit_card.data_clock: None. Finite enumeration, no sampling, no LLM. Maps and menus specified before the run.
material_assumptions: Gold semantics is Paper E's empirical rule with the menu as an argument.
Menu-blind means: a function of (Y, q, edges) that never enumerates the menu.
κ_cheap is Paper E decide, frozen.
The tie-break is fewest fibres then lexicographic name, as in Paper F.

objects.gold_of_menu: (CaseSpec, worlds, Menu) → {restore, quotient, transport, noop, broken}
objects.flip: a case with gold_of_menu(-, MENU_BASE) ≠ gold_of_menu(-, MENU_EXT)

mathematical_claim.types_domains_units: X = {0,1}^4, 16 worlds. Fibre counts are integers: q_pair01 and q_pair23 have 12 fibres. Menus are ordered tuples of screen ids.
mathematical_claim.exact_claim: There exists a case c with gold_base(c) = noop and gold_ext(c) = quotient. Hence gold is not a function of (Y, q, edges), so for every function f of (Y, q, edges) there is a menu under which f mismatches gold on c. Also: the five-field signature partition has a mixed-gold bucket under MENU_BASE and no mixed-gold bucket under MENU_EXT on this suite.
mathematical_claim.quantifiers: Existential for the flip and the base collision. Universal over all 34 rows for kappa_screen exactness. Universal over all menu-blind functions in the impossibility reading (a two-point separation argument, enumerated).
mathematical_claim.assumptions: Gold semantics fixed as registered. Menus disclosed. No sampling.
mathematical_claim.identification_conditions: kappa_screen_menu is identified as Theorem 4 plus the disclosed total order, per menu. It is not identified as a new primitive.
mathematical_claim.derivation_dependencies: Paper E gold_of and decide. Paper F kappa_screen. CommonSuffScreen / Theorem 4. The impossibility step is the two-valued-function separation: one input, two required outputs.
mathematical_claim.coordinate_invariance: Reversal (3,2,1,0) sends first_bit↔last_bit and pair_eq↔pair23, q_stab0↔q_stab_last, q_pair01↔q_pair23. Action-level naturality is required. Chosen-screen naturality is measured and may fail on ties broken by name; failures are recorded.
mathematical_claim.edge_limiting_null_cases: If no flip occurs the categorical kill fails and the verdict must not claim it. If κ_screen misses, the no-function reading reopens and the verdict says so. broken never appears because q_id is in every menu.

compute.sampling: Finite {0,1}^4 enumeration, 17 cases, two menus. No sampling.

claim_boundary: Accepted only as: gold is menu-relative on this harness, so no menu-blind κ of any signature width is correct across menus; the five-field rule's collision and correctness are menu-relative; κ_screen stays exact per menu; the name tie-break is not relabel-natural on ties. Not a new master object. Not a refit. Not an LLM. Not Paper G.
